consensus_summary: All four consensus responses identify the field's primary symbolic meaning as the world — the sphere of humanity in which God's word is sown and the eschatological harvest occurs — grounded in Jesus' explicit interpretation in Matthew 13:38 ('the field is the world'). Common alternatives include the mission/harvest field of souls, the human heart as soil, and the church as God's cultivated field (1 Cor 3:9).
book_summary: The book identifies the field as the world, explicitly citing Jesus' own decoding (Matt 13:38), sown with the seed of the word and reaped at harvest. It adds two elaborations within that frame: the unreaped edge of the field where the poor and stranger glean (Lev 19:9-10), and the hidden treasure bought with the whole field (echoing Matt 13:44).
consensus_core_identification: The field is the world — the whole human realm where God's kingdom is sown and judged at harvest, per Jesus' explicit interpretation in Matthew 13:38.
book_core_identification: The field is the world, per Jesus' own decoding (Matt 13:38), the sown-and-reaped human sphere.
boundary_disagreement: None. The book's additions — the gleaning margins for the poor and stranger, and the treasure-in-the-field motif — are elaborations layered onto the same world-referent, not restrictions or expansions of what the field denotes. The gleaning detail (Lev 19:9-10) extends the imagery ethically (mercy at the world's edges) without altering the identification, and the treasure detail matches an alternative already noted in Response A (Matt 13:44 field as the world purchased whole).
material_contradiction: None. Both the book and the consensus rest on the identical dominical key, Matthew 13:38.
rationale: The book's core identification is verbatim the consensus core: the field is the world, and the book even flags this as 'Jesus' own decoding,' the same warrant every consensus response cites. The added imagery (gleaning corners, hidden treasure) enriches rather than modifies the referent; the treasure reading appears in Response A's alternatives and the gleaning detail is a compatible ethical extension of the world-as-field. There is no boundary change, narrowing, or replacement, so MATCH is the correct verdict.
strongest_objection: One could argue the gleaning motif (Lev 19:9-10) introduces a materially new dimension — the world's 'unreaped edge' as a locus of mercy for the poor and stranger — that no consensus response mentions, potentially warranting REFINED. But this addition does not change the extension or boundary of what 'field' identifies; it is homiletic elaboration on the same referent.
